question: The first permanent settlements of the Stone Age, where agriculture began, are characteristic of which period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neolithic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Neolithic (New Stone Age) marks the beginning of agriculture and the first permanent settlements, because crops needed cultivation and care (नवपाषाण — स्थायी बस्तियाँ और कृषि)

 

• Four main Neolithic features: agriculture, domestication of animals, polished stone tools and pottery.

 

• Mehrgarh (c. 7000 BC) gives the earliest evidence of agriculture.

 

• The beginning of agriculture led to permanent settlements.

 

• Settled village life changes everything else too: houses, storage pits, pottery and ownership of land follow from the need to stay near the crops, so the Neolithic is often called the beginning of village life.

 

• In sequence terms, the Mesolithic prepared the ground by introducing early cultivation, but it is the Neolithic that fully established farming and villages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neolithic means New Stone Age, the stage in which agriculture first appeared.

 

• Mehrgarh is the earliest agricultural site known in the subcontinent.

 

• Palaeolithic hunters moved with the animals, while Neolithic farmers stayed.

 

• The Chalcolithic keeps farming but adds copper tools.

 

• Because the Neolithic brought permanent villages, it is described as the first stage where humans produced food rather than only collecting it, a contrast that can be asked in comparison questions.

 

NOTE

 

• Palaeolithic (Option 2): Palaeolithic people were mobile hunter-gatherers with no agriculture, so they could not have had permanent agricultural settlements. Palaeolithic people were mobile hunter-gatherers without settlements. Their camps were temporary because they moved with game and wild plants, unlike the farming villages that appear only later.

 

• Mesolithic (Option 3): Mesolithic people only started staying longer in one place and began early cultivation; permanent farming settlements came with the Neolithic. Mesolithic people only began staying longer in one place; settlements were not yet agricultural villages.

 

• Chalcolithic (Option 4): Chalcolithic is the later copper-using phase that followed the Neolithic, so the first permanent settlements are not its characteristic. Chalcolithic is the later copper-using phase, after the Neolithic.

question:
Consider the following statements about Mehrgarh:

1. It is located in Baluchistan (Pakistan).

2. It is dated to about 7000 BC.

3. It gives the earliest evidence of agriculture.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three are correct: Mehrgarh is in Baluchistan (Pakistan), dated to 7000 BC, and provides the earliest evidence of agriculture (मेहरगढ़ — बलूचिस्तान, 7000 ई.पू., कृषि के प्राचीनतम साक्ष्य)

 

• It is a key Neolithic site.

 

• A sickle ('hasiya') was recovered here.

 

• It was known in its own time as the 'Bread Basket' (Roti ki Tokari).

 

• When a statement-based question lists Mehrgarh facts, check all three attributes together: place (Baluchistan), time (about 7000 BC) and significance (earliest evidence of agriculture). Missing even one means choosing a wrong option.

 

• All three statements together describe the same site, so the answer is the option that accepts every statement without leaving anything out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mehrgarh lies in the Kachi plain of Baluchistan near the Bolan pass.

 

• It was excavated by a French team led by Jean-Francois Jarrige.

 

• Mehrgarh precedes the Indus Valley Civilisation and is often seen as its forerunner.

 

• Wheat and barley are the crops associated with this early farming.

 

• A statement question on Mehrgarh can add distractors such as Punjab, Gujarat or 3000 BC; the three true anchors to remember are Baluchistan, about 7000 BC and the earliest evidence of agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Although statements 1 and 2 do match the notes, dropping statement 3 is an error: Mehrgarh is the site with the earliest evidence of agriculture, which is exactly why it was called the Bread Basket.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): The pair of statements 2 and 3 is sound, but dropping statement 1 is an error: Mehrgarh lies in Baluchistan, now in Pakistan, on the Kachi plain near the Bolan pass.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statements 1 and 3 hold good, but dropping statement 2 is an error: Mehrgarh is dated to about 7000 BC, which makes it far older than the Indus cities.

question: What was the first metal to be used by humans, leading to the Chalcolithic period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Copper (Cu) was the very first metal humans discovered; the Chalcolithic period takes its name from it (chalco = copper) (ताँबा — पहली धातु, ताम्रपाषाण काल)

 

• In the Chalcolithic phase copper objects were used besides stone along with stone tools.

 

• It is also called the Metal Age in the notes' four-phase scheme.

 

• Sites include Ganeshwar, Ahar, Jorwe, Inamgaon and Navdatoli.

 

• The sequence of materials is stone, then copper, then bronze, then iron. Copper comes first because it occurs as native metal and melts at a lower temperature than iron, so it could be worked earlier.

 

• This fact links the Chalcolithic Age to the first metal; remember that the age name itself, with chalco as copper, answers this question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Copper is soft and was shaped by hammering before smelting was learnt.

 

• The alloy of copper and tin is bronze, and it came later.

 

• Iron needs very high temperatures to smelt, so it was adopted later.

 

• The first metal and the first pet animal are two firsts often confused in lists.

 

• The notes call the Chalcolithic age the Metal Age and mention that copper is the first metal; this link between the age name, its root word and the first metal is a frequent short question.

 

NOTE

 

• Iron (Option 1): Iron is a later metal that came into use after copper and bronze; it did not define the Chalcolithic period. Iron was discovered much later than copper.

 

• Gold (Option 2): Gold was known to early people, but it is a soft metal not used for tools, and it was not the first metal that gave the Chalcolithic its name. Gold was known but it is not the first metal that defined the Chalcolithic period.

 

• Bronze (Option 3): Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin and could be made only after copper was already known, so it was not the first metal. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, made after copper was already known.

question: The term 'Chalcolithic' is used for which age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper and Stone Age.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chalcolithic means the Copper and Stone Age: chalco = copper, lithic = stone, so people used both copper and stone tools (ताम्रपाषाण युग — ताँबा और पत्थर)

 

• It follows the Neolithic and is called the Metal Age in the notes.

 

• Copper was the first metal humans discovered.

 

• Chalcolithic cultures were mostly rural, with painted pottery.

 

• Chalcolithic is sometimes compared with the Neolithic: the Neolithic is purely a stone age with farming, while the Chalcolithic keeps farming and stone tools but adds copper objects, giving a mixed technology.

 

• The Greek roots chalkos (copper) and lithos (stone) are the best way to recall the meaning if you forget the English definition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The notes call the Chalcolithic the Metal Age.

 

• Chalcolithic cultures were generally village-based, practising farming and herding with copper and stone.

 

• Sites include Ganeshwar, Ahar, Jorwe, Inamgaon and Navtadoli.

 

• Chalco is Greek for copper, a clue for decoding the term.

 

• If an option mentions bronze, iron or silver with the word stone, it describes a different age or none at all, so only the pairing of copper with stone matches the Greek word parts chalco and lithic.

 

NOTE

 

• Bronze and Stone Age (Option 2): Bronze and Stone Age is not a recognised label; bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, while chalco refers to copper alone. Bronze is not the metal indicated by the word 'chalco'.

 

• Bronze and Iron Age (Option 3): Bronze and Iron Age refers to later metal-using periods, which came after the Chalcolithic and are different from it. Bronze and Iron Age are later metal ages, not Chalcolithic.

 

• Silver and Bronze Age (Option 4): Silver and Bronze Age is not a recognised stage of prehistory; chalco never refers to silver. Silver is not involved in the term Chalcolithic. Silver is a precious metal used for ornaments in later periods and never gave its name to a prehistoric age.

question: Which of the following correctly lists the Indian prehistoric phases in chronological order?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palaeolithic - Mesolithic - Neolithic - Chalcolithic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct order is Palaeolithic (Old), Mesolithic (Middle), Neolithic (New) and Chalcolithic (Metal Age) (पुरापाषाण, मध्यपाषाण, नवपाषाण, ताम्रपाषाण — कालक्रम)

 

• Tools change from large pebble tools to microliths to polished tools to copper.

 

• Subsistence changes from hunting-gathering to early cultivation to agriculture to metal use.

 

• Meso is middle, so it must come between Palaeo (old) and Neo (new).

 

• The order is linked with a chain of change: wild food, then early cultivation, then farming, then metal. If you remember what each phase added, the sequence cannot be reversed.

 

• The right order follows the notes: Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic and the Metal Age, in increasing technological advance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Palaeolithic is before 10000 BC, and Mesolithic about 10000 to 6000 BC.

 

• Neolithic brought farming and pottery.

 

• Chalcolithic added copper.

 

• The order can be recalled as old, middle, new, copper.

 

• For sequence questions, anchor on the two extremes first: Palaeolithic is the earliest and Chalcolithic the latest of the four phases, which immediately eliminates every option that begins with another age.

 

NOTE

 

• Mesolithic - Palaeolithic - Neolithic - Chalcolithic (Option 1): This puts the Middle Stone Age before the Old Stone Age, which is impossible since Palaeolithic is the first phase. Mesolithic cannot precede the Old Stone Age.

 

• Palaeolithic - Neolithic - Mesolithic - Chalcolithic (Option 2): This puts the New Stone Age before the Middle Stone Age; Mesolithic lies between Palaeolithic and Neolithic. Neolithic cannot come before the Middle Stone Age.

 

• Neolithic - Palaeolithic - Mesolithic - Chalcolithic (Option 4): This puts the New Stone Age at the very start, before the Old Stone Age, which reverses the sequence. Neolithic cannot come before the Old Stone Age.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

• A is true, but R is false (Option 3): R is true, as crops need cultivation and care, so people had to stay at one place; hence R cannot be called false. R is true, so 'R is false' fails.

 

• A is false, but R is true (Option 4): A is true, since the beginning of agriculture led to permanent settlements, so the assertion cannot be called false. A is true, so 'A is false' fails.

question: Which tools are a characteristic feature of the Neolithic Age?

• The Neolithic follows the Mesolithic microlith phase.

• Polishing means grinding a stone tool against a hard surface to give it a smooth, sharp edge. Such tools were more durable than chipped ones and were useful in clearing land and farming.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

• They were used in farming and wood work.

 

• Microliths are Mesolithic and handaxes are Palaeolithic.

NOTE

 

• Microliths (Option 1): Microliths are the tiny stone tools of the Mesolithic Age, usually not longer than five centimetres, and they precede the Neolithic. Microliths are the characteristic tools of the Mesolithic Age.

 

• Handaxes and cleavers (Option 2): Handaxes and cleavers are the large tools of the Lower Palaeolithic, the earliest stage of the Old Stone Age. Handaxes and cleavers are Lower Palaeolithic tools.
